   175	
   176	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   177	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
   178	/-- Construct the certificate package after a genuine finitely generated descent stage.
   179	
   180	`hW₀` is the fibre-divisor/H¹ antecedent at the stage and `hdegree` is the corresponding
   181	class-degree calculation.  Neither field mentions the desired H¹/H⁰/rank conclusions.  The
   182	Noetherian instance is created only for `B₀`; the result is over the original, unrestricted
   183	ring `B` by the canonical datum base-change equivalence. -/
   184	noncomputable def of_descent_stage
   185	    {B₀ : Subalgebra k B} (hfg : B₀.FG)
   186	    (D₀ : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (↥B₀) pi)
   187	    (hbc : D₀.baseChange (B' := B) = D)
   188	    (hπ : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   189	    (hW₀ : D₀.FibreH1Witness)
   190	    (hdegree : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (↥B₀),
   191	      classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   192	        (D₀.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (genus C : ℤ)) :
   193	    RankOneFamilyCertificates D := by
   194	  subst D
   195	  letI : IsNoetherianRing (↥B₀) := hfg.isNoetherianRing
   196	  have hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (↥B₀),
   197	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D₀).H1 ⊗[↥B₀] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   198	    intro p
   199	    exact D₀.subsingleton_pairH1_tensor_of_fibreWitness hW₀
   200	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   201	  obtain ⟨h1₀, hfin₀, hproj₀⟩ :=
   202	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.descentRigidEngine hfg D₀ hπ hfib
   203	  have hpair₀ : Subsingleton (datumPair D₀).H1 :=
   204	    (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff D₀).mpr h1₀
   205	  have hrank₀ : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (↥B₀),
   206	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D₀.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   207	    intro p
   208	    haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   209	      instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   210	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   211	        (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘
   212	          Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   213	      instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   214	    haveI : QuasiCompact
   215	        (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘
   216	          Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   217	      instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   218	    haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   219	        (Sheaf.HModule
   220	          ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   221	      instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   222	    haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   223	        (Sheaf.HModule
   224	          ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   225	      instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   226	    exact BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one D₀ (n := genus C) hπ
   227	      (chi_moduleKSheaf C) hfib p (hdegree p)
   228	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule D₀.sheaf 0
   229	  letI : Module.Finite (↥B₀) Q := hfin₀
   230	  letI : Module.Projective (↥B₀) Q := hproj₀
   231	  let e : B ⊗[↥B₀] Q ≃ₗ[B]
   232	      Sheaf.HModule (D₀.baseChange (B' := B)).sheaf 0 :=
   233	    D₀.datumH0BaseChange B hpair₀
   234	  letI : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[↥B₀] Q) := by infer_instance
   235	  letI : Module.Projective B (B ⊗[↥B₀] Q) := by infer_instance
   236	  refine {
   237	    h1_vanishing := D₀.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange B hpair₀
   238	    h0_finite := Module.Finite.equiv e
   239	    h0_projective := Module.Projective.of_equiv e
   240	    h0_rank_one := ?_ }
   241	  intro p
   242	  rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv e, Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange]
   243	  exact hrank₀ (p.comap (algebraMap (↥B₀) B))
   244

    10	/-!
    11	# Lambda-tied assembly of rank-one family certificates
    12	
    13	This file is the Picard-side consumer of `RankOneFamilyCertificates`.  It does not choose a
    14	module: the certificate and the native presentation are both attached to the displayed cocycle
    15	datum.  The cover representative and its equality with the displayed lambda class provide the
    16	Picard tie, while arbitrary-cartesian native pushforward base change remains a separate geometric
    17	input.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	set_option autoImplicit false
    21	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    26	  CartesianMonoidalCategory

    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    30	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    31	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    37	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

    39	namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation

    41	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    42	
    43	/-! ## The literal native consumer -/
    44	
    45	/-- Assemble the native presentation from certificates for the same displayed cocycle datum.
    46	
    47	The equalities `hrep` and `hclass` tie the datum to the requested lambda class.  All four
    48	cohomological fields are projected from `cert`, whose modules are definitionally the H-modules
    49	of `D.sheaf`; no unrelated or pre-certified target module can enter.  The all-cartesian native
    50	pushforward comparison is intentionally an explicit argument until its protected producer lands.
    51	-/
    52	noncomputable def ofCertificates
    53	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
    54	    (x : descentClasses C E)
    55	    (hrep : PicEtAff.mk C E x = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1)
    56	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C E.Carrier pi)
    57	    (hclass :
    58	      (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) =
    59	        relPicMk C (overSpec k E.Carrier) D.cechPicClass)
    60	    (hpush :
    61	      ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    62	        (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of E.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    63	        (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C E.Carrier)
    64	        (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    65	          (relCurve C E.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of E.Carrier)) g),
    66	        IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app D.nativeModule))
    67	    (cert : RankOneFamilyCertificates D) :
    68	    PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam :=
    69	  { cover := E
    70	    representative := x
    71	    represents := hrep
    72	    datum := D
    73	    datum_class := hclass
    74	    native_pushforward_base_change := hpush
    75	    h1_vanishing := cert.h1_vanishing
    76	    h0_finite := cert.h0_finite
    77	    h0_projective := cert.h0_projective
    78	    h0_rank_one := cert.h0_rank_one }
    79	
    80	end PicRankOneNativePresentation

60	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    61	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    62	
    63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    64	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    65	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
    66	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    67	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    68	
    69	/-- **CHART-U(b), the datum-level witness-locus openness** (`w4-datc` §3.3 step (3)):
    70	for a pinned basic-open cocycle datum `D` over the affine base `B`, the locus of primes
    71	`q` at which the fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` has an effective witness divisor with
    72	vanishing `H¹` is open in `Spec B`.
    73	
    74	This is `datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` (the single audited openness engine,
    75	Noetherian-free) read in the class/witness form of the `chartLocus` predicate through
    76	the two-way datum dictionary
    77	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6):
    78	pointwise the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`
    79	is exactly the existence of such a witness. -/
    80	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing
    81	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
    82	    IsOpen {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
    83	      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
    84	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
    85	            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
    86	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    87	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
    88	                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
    89	  have hset : {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
    90	      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
    91	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
    92	            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
    93	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    94	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
    95	                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)}
    96	      = {p : PrimeSpectrum B |
    97	          Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)} := by
    98	    refine Set.ext fun q => ?_
    99	    exact (D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness q.asIdeal.ResidueField).symm
   100	  rw [hset]
   101	  exact datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing D hπ
   102	
   103	/-! ## The openness transport (CHART-U(b) link 2, topological half)
   104	
   105	The engine produces the open witness locus over the étale carrier `Spec B` (or, on the
   106	away pieces, over `Spec (Localization.Away f)`).  CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii)
   107	(`w4-datb` §1.6, "the Kleiman tex 2204-2244 step, now one `IsOpenMap` application")
   108	carries it down to the test base `Spec A` along the étale carrier map, which is open
   109	and surjective.  The pure-topology core of that step is below; the remaining
   110	mathematical content of link 2 is the *fibre-field invariance* that identifies the
   111	preimage of the base locus with the carrier locus (`κ(q)/κ(p)` a separable extension;
   112	`isH1VanishingAt_comap_away_iff` is the landed avatar for the away case). -/
   113	
   114	/-- **Openness descends along an open continuous surjection**: if `f` is continuous,
   115	open, and surjective and `f ⁻¹' V` is open, then `V` is open — because
   116	`V = f '' (f ⁻¹' V)` (surjectivity) and `f` carries opens to opens.  This is the
   117	topological core of CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii). -/
   118	theorem isOpen_of_isOpen_preimage_of_isOpenMap_surjective
   119	    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : X → Y}
   120	    (hcont : Continuous f) (hopen : IsOpenMap f) (hsurj : Function.Surjective f)
   240	  canonical instance and the predicate is not invariant under regrading the field over `A`;
   241	* the only genuine content is the transport across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, which is
   242	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` applied to the isomorphism, in the tower
   243	  `A → κ(q) → (Spec A).residueField t` supplied by
   244	  `algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors`. -/
   245	theorem isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField
   246	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   247	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) :
   248	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   249	      D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} := by
   250	  -- The two loci are the SAME set of the SAME type: `↥(overSpec k A).left` is
   251	  -- `PrimeSpectrum A` definitionally, so only the fibre field differs, and the predicate is
   252	  -- invariant under the isomorphism between the two readings of it.
   253	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   254	        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)}
   255	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum A |
   256	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
   257	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
   258	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   259	                    D.cechPicClass
   260	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   261	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
   262	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
   263	    refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
   264	    -- the comparison iso as an algebra structure, and its tower over `A`
   265	    letI : Algebra (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
   266	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
   267	      ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.toAlgebra
   268	    haveI : IsScalarTower A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
   269	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
   270	      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors t)
   271	    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
   272	      (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
   273	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).symm
   274	  rw [hset]
   275	  exact D.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ
   276	
   277	/-! ## Transports (0) and (iii): the identification with the landed locus -/
   278	
   279	/-- **`chartLocus` over an affine test is the witness locus of a presenting datum.**
   280	
   281	This is transport (0) (the class-indexation, landed as `cechWitnessLocus`) composed with
   282	transport (iii) (locality on the affine test, here trivial because the test *is* affine),
   283	run against the presentation hypothesis.  The content is entirely the translation between
   284	the two ways the tree indexes a fibre — by a point of the test object's space
   285	(`Over.testPoint`, the `chartLocus` side) and by a prime of the test algebra
   286	(`q.asIdeal.ResidueField`, the engine side).
   287	
   288	The translation is available precisely because `Over.testPointField` at a point of
   289	`(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and `q.asIdeal.ResidueField` at the corresponding prime are
   290	the same field up to the canonical `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the witness predicate is
   291	invariant under field isomorphism over the base (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`
   292	applied to an isomorphism). -/
   293	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing
   294	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   295	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
   296	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
   297	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
   298	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
   299	  (hpres t).symm
   300	
   301	/-! ## The keystone, conditionally -/
   302	
   303	variable (C π) in
   304	/-- **`isOpen_chartLocus`, given the shifted-datum presentation** (dat-b row B-4's keystone,
   305	over an affine test).
   306	
   307	The proof is the route of record with the one missing link supplied as `hpres`: rewrite
   308	membership of `chartLocus` as the datum's witness predicate at the residue field of the
   309	point (the presentation), then quote the landed datum-level openness
   310	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` — itself the engine
   311	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` read through the GAP-6 dictionary.
   312	
   313	The general-test statement follows from this one by the affine-piece locality of the
   314	(b-amendment)'s transport (iii): `chartLocus` over `T` meets each affine open `U ⊆ T.left` in
   315	`chartLocus` over `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` (by `picEtMap_chartTwist` along
   316	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`), and a set that is open in every member of an open cover is open.
   317	That last step is `isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter`-style bookkeeping and needs no new
   318	mathematics; it is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis
   319	*per affine piece*, which is a statement about the general test and therefore belongs with
   320	the honesty/presentation obligations named in the header table. -/
   321	theorem isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   322	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   323	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
   324	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) :
   325	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   326	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)} := by
   327	  -- The engine's open set is indexed by primes of `A`; the locus is indexed by points of

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

      "body": "[persistent] HUMAN DECISION, BINDING (2026-07-28): DivFamZar is widened to ARBITRARY AFFINE OPEN pieces. R2 of I-0346 is chosen and closed; R1 (the GL_2/Aut(P1) route) is NOT to be built.\n\nTHE RULE, for any session on the DD-R certificate lane or its consumers:\n\n 1. DO NOT BUILD THE GL_2(k) ACTION ON P1. Roadmap leaf AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.p1-aut stays pending and DEPRIORITISED \u2014 not rejected (R1 may still accelerate the large-field case one day), but no session spends time on it, and no consumer may be written against it. Same for any descent work whose only purpose is to rescue R1.\n\n 2. The widening target: FinCoverData s pieces become arbitrary affine opens rather than basic opens of a FIXED PAIR of pinned P1 charts. Justification to use, not to re-derive: supp D is finite over R, hence lies in a single affine open of C x_k Spec R (Stacks 0B8B); spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 4 carries the argument.\n\n 3. THE CHART-WISE PARTITIONS OF UNITY ARE WHAT HAS TO GO. Per-piece swallow-or-miss needs only openness (DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean uses only openness); it is the partitions that upgrade inside one piece to inside one chart. Removing them will break consumers \u2014 repair the consumers deliberately, and do not smuggle the old typing back in by typing pieces INTO the charts (DivisorFamily.lean h0/h1/pieces is exactly the pattern that made the previous cheaper option vacuous).\n\n 4. TWO OBLIGATIONS THE WIDENING RELOCATES RATHER THAN REMOVES, both to be discharged explicitly and neither to be hidden inside a LocalEquations: (i) fibrewise-finite support, which must come from the seed s own degree data; (ii) whatever the old fixed-pair confinement was silently supplying to the certificate clauses.\n\n 5. THE STANDING NEGATIVE RESULTS REMAIN BINDING, all established by predecessor sessions and adversarially checked. Chart-avoid is NO. The counterexample is FIELD-INDEPENDENT, so enlarging the field is not an escape. And the sharp form to quote: NO repair that keeps the pieces inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of P1 can work. The joint-cover variant is refuted (leaf ...joint-cover, rejected) \u2014 do not retry it.\n\nWHY R2 AND NOT A FIELD-SIZE HYPOTHESIS: archon-protected.yaml freezes the arbitrary-field statement, so |P1(k)| >= n+2 would answer a different question. R2 is the only field-uniform fix. The sharpness result (leaf ...field-size, done) stands and needs no further human input.\n\nFull reasoning: I-0346 (human comment, 2026-07-28). Executing task: ajcr-cert-r2.",
